reason: The text (Exodus 3:7-8) explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's profound empathy for the Hebrew people, not indifference. Yahweh states: 'I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters. For I know their sorrows. And I will come down to deliver them from the hand of Egypt.' The passage emphasizes Yahweh's awareness of the people's suffering (עֳנִי עַמִּי - affliction of my people), their cries (צַעֲקָתָם - their cry), and their pain (מַכְאֹבָיו - their sorrows). Moses is called as an instrument to execute this deliverance, but the entire theological focus is on Yahweh's compassion for the collective people, not merely for leaders. The commissioning of a leader serves the people's liberation, not the reverse.
